title: Calibration review
description: Review calibration range and independent evidence for a reported result.
body:
When a quantitative result depends on calibration standards.

## Evidence to gather

Eligible standards, sample response, applicable method revision and independent checks where relevant

## Review procedure

1. Identify the decision being made. Locating a response within the standards, estimating a quantity and releasing a result under a lab method require different evidence. Retrieve the method revision in effect for this run, the eligible standards, the sample, their units and the relationship fitted. Compare responses on the measured scale. Record the observed bounds and any narrower method limits, including their boundary convention.

2. For a claim about accuracy or release, look for evidence independent of the observations used to fit the curve. A check material with a known assigned value can test a prediction. Compare the measured or back-calculated value with its assignment using the applicable method’s rule, units and tolerance. Identify which run and materials the check covers. A close fit, a repeat of an unknown, or a proposal to extend the curve answers a different question.

3. Give separate conclusions for range, the independent check, and the requested decision. Report a derived quantity only in units supported by the calibration. If method versions or records disagree, use documented applicability and authority to resolve them. If unresolved, show how the decision depends on the competing records and name the evidence that would resolve it. Cite the standards defining the bounds and the records supporting the decision.

## Expected result

Range and check assessments with a decision scoped to the method

title: Evidence summary
description: Trace a reported result to its readings, method, and review decisions.
body:
When preparing a record for independent review.

## Evidence to gather

Run history, source readings, and reviewer decisions

## Review procedure

1. Begin with a specific result or reporting decision and its run identifier. Work backwards through the supplied evidence to the sample and raw observations, the measurement context, the versioned method, and any decisions linking one run to another. Keep references local to the run unless an explicit relationship identifies a predecessor.

2. Reconstruct the sequence using recorded facts. Keep raw values, derived values, reviewer decisions and agent findings distinct. For a time course, cite the recorded time unit and the points supporting any claimed trend. Endpoints alone support an endpoint change; they cannot establish a monotonic trace. For a diluted repeat, distinguish the measured sample concentration from the original concentration reported after correction.

3. Write a short account in which each consequential claim has a source field or record reference. Mark gaps explicitly, including a missing reviewer decision or unidentified instrument when relevant to the requested claim. A connector listed in a run briefing is configuration metadata; count retrieved records as evidence only when they are actually supplied. On rereview, preserve earlier summaries and identify which new or corrected evidence changed the conclusion.

## Expected result

A summary with references to the underlying records

title: Method comparison
description: Compare the method revisions and settings recorded for two runs.
body:
When a comparison relies on the runs using comparable methods.

## Evidence to gather

Two method records

## Review procedure

1. Identify the two method records requested for comparison. Capture both revision labels and their sources. Prefer the snapshots tied to the two runs. If only today’s library version is supplied, identify the missing historical version and leave its changes unassessed.

2. Align fields by scientific meaning. Compare measurement conditions, units, analysis equations, applicability ranges, and reporting rules to the extent recorded. Separate a unit conversion from a physical change, a wording change from a new requirement, and an omitted field from a known deletion. For example, 0.595 µm and 595 nm represent the same wavelength. A change to a dilution used in one repeat belongs to execution history unless the method revision itself changes.

3. Report before and after values with both references. State how a material difference could affect comparison of the results, and label its actual effect unknown unless run evidence establishes it. If two records carry the same revision label but disagree on a field, surface the identity conflict for the method owner. On rereview, retain one observation for each revision pair and changed field. Leave selecting an approved revision to the researcher.

## Expected result

A list of changes to parameters and interpretation

title: Method reference
description: Identify the method and revision cited by a run.
body:
When a record identifies the procedure used.

## Evidence to gather

Method name and revision from the run briefing.

## Review procedure

1. Identify the method for this run. Start with the original or repeat run’s saved briefing. Extract the exact method name and revision. If a method record is linked and supplied, follow that link and compare its identifier and revision with the citation. Treat titles found by text similarity as possible matches only.

2. Judge identification separately from content. A name and revision establish what the briefing cites. Claim that a clause was inspected only when its versioned text is available. For example, a briefing that says “Absorbance method v1.0” can identify v1.0 even when the library now displays v2.0. If two supplied records plausibly match the same citation, leave the target unresolved and identify both candidates.

3. Return the run identifier, cited method and revision, and the record or field that supports each. Mark a blank revision unassessed. When a supplied linked revision conflicts with the briefing, anchor the finding to the inconsistent reference. Suggest that the researcher identify the intended record. On rereview, compare the same citation and carry forward existing findings once per affected field. Preserve the as-run citation.

## Expected result

Method identification status with the available briefing references.

title: Run setup completeness
description: Check whether the recorded setup includes the fields needed for the stated measurement.
body:
Before a run or when auditing its original briefing.

## Evidence to gather

Run objective, project, method revision and the measurement settings required by that method.

## Review procedure

1. Establish the intended measurement before execution. Read the saved objective, project, and versioned method reference. From the supplied method, identify the fields essential to interpreting this measurement. For the illustrative absorbance methods, the briefing includes a wavelength in nm. For a different method, use its stated requirements and units.

2. Inspect each required field for presence and meaning. Record the field, value, unit, and applicable method clause where available. A positive wavelength makes that field usable; it does not establish that the method calls for that wavelength. A missing wavelength leaves the check unassessed. A recorded value of zero nm is a concrete finding. If a referenced method is unavailable, report which briefing checks you completed and which method-specific checks need its text.

3. Return a readiness note with the required field that needs attention, the evidence, and the smallest clarification that would settle it. If all supplied checks pass, state their limited scope. Keep this decision advisory and leave starting the run to the existing approval flow. On a revised draft, compare changed fields with the original finding and retain any still-open gaps.

## Expected result

Briefing readiness with field references and any missing or invalid setup.

title: Instrument record
description: Trace an equipment reference to the measurement and recorded operating settings.
body:
When a result depends on the instrument used.

## Evidence to gather

Equipment reference, applicable method, operating settings and the associated run record.

## Review procedure

1. Trace the measurement to the equipment identified at run start. Use the instrument field captured with the run. If it carries a stable instrument or asset ID, use that ID to locate a supplied inventory record. Record a human-readable label at the level of specificity the evidence supports.

2. Cross-check the recorded instrument, method, and measurement setting against the supplied records. For an absorbance run, cite the recorded wavelength and its unit. A briefing can name a UV–Vis spectrometer without identifying which physical unit was used. If an inventory lists two instruments with that label, report the identity ambiguity. A current inventory entry alone cannot establish historical availability, maintenance status, or which instrument produced a reading.

3. Attach the identification result to the run’s instrument field. Cite the matching ID if present and identify the exact missing detail when stronger provenance is needed. Flag an observed identifier conflict separately from missing context. On rereview, reconcile the previous finding against the same run and the newly supplied evidence. Leave historical readings and equipment settings intact.

## Expected result

A cited start-record check identifying any missing context.

title: Dilution calculation
description: Trace a reported concentration through its calibration and dilution correction.
body:
When a reported quantity includes a recorded dilution.

## Evidence to gather

Recorded sample response, applicable calibration, dilution factor and reported concentration.

## Review procedure

1. Trace the reported value back to the diluted sample. Identify the repeat run, standard concentration–response pairs, sample response, reporting units, recorded dilution factor and its convention. Distinguish a result for the measured aliquot from a result for the original sample. Use the recorded preparation factor for calculation; a planned or approved factor is evidence of intent.

2. Check whether the measured response falls within the calibrated region. Use the method’s recorded curve and conversion rules. For the illustrative B12 method, locate adjacent standards that bracket the response on a monotonic curve and interpolate linearly. If the bracket is ambiguous, units conflict, or the method requires model parameters that are absent, stop with the missing input. Outside the usable range, inspect whether concentration was withheld and flag an extrapolated numeric report.

3. Show the audit trail in units. In the supplied B12 example, 0.650 AU interpolates to 7.5 µM in the measured aliquot. A recorded twofold dilution gives 15.0 µM in the original sample. Check the report against its stated target and precision; applying the same factor again would give 30.0 µM. Anchor the discrepancy to the reported value, identify the first unsupported step, and retain the calculation as an advisory review.

## Expected result

A cited comparison or a determination that concentration should be withheld.

title: Method adherence
description: Compare a reported decision with a specific clause of the method used.
body:
When both a result and its applicable method are supplied.

## Evidence to gather

Versioned method clause, observations for this run, and the reported decision.

## Review procedure

1. Select one explicit obligation from the method revision associated with this run. Identify its trigger, required behavior, and the run record where the behavior would be observable. If the method text is unavailable, assess only rules explicitly supplied for this fixture. State their scope.

2. Compare the observed decision to that obligation. In the illustrative B12 workflow, an out-of-range reading requires concentration to be withheld. A flagged measurement with an explicit withholding decision follows that rule. A numeric concentration for the same out-of-range reading contradicts it. An absent result field leaves the decision unknown. Treat ambiguous or missing evidence separately from a demonstrated contradiction.

3. For each contradiction, anchor one finding to the affected decision and cite the method clause and run evidence. Explain the expected and observed behavior in language a researcher can check. If the supplied decision is consistent, record the checked scope without adding an issue. On rereview, identify the prior finding by run, rule and affected field. Update the advisory status only when new evidence addresses it. Preserve human comments, approval history, and the original measurement.

## Expected result

A cited assessment of whether the recorded decision follows the identified clause.

title: Repeat comparison
description: Check a repeat against its original observation and the authorized change.
body:
When a repeat or remeasurement is linked to an earlier result.

## Evidence to gather

Linked original and repeat records, comparable measurements and the authorized change.

## Review procedure

1. Establish the lineage of the repeat. Find the explicitly linked original run, the reason it was flagged, the reviewer’s decision, and the repeat it authorized. Match sample identifiers when the records supply them. A neighboring run in a list is insufficient to establish that link. If the predecessor or approval is ambiguous, stop the authorization check and cite the unresolved link.

2. Compare what was requested, what was authorized, and what the repeat records as performed. Cite factors, units or changed conditions alongside both run IDs. Use each run’s own standards and method revision to evaluate its outcome. An in-range repeat at a recorded fourfold dilution can still conflict with approval for a twofold dilution. Conversely, a repeat can follow the approved change and still yield an out-of-range reading.

3. Return two conclusions: whether the documented change matches the approval, and whether the repeat addresses the original finding. Mark either unassessed when its evidence is missing. Cite the decision and both observations and keep an unresolved discrepancy visible even if the other check passes. A single repeat establishes the outcome of that repeat; use a separate study design to assess broader reproducibility. On rereview, update the finding for this run pair while preserving its approval trail.

## Expected result

A comparison of expected and observed changes with citations and unresolved differences.

title: Data intake and provenance
description: Trace observations to sources and assess how gaps or corrections affect the claim.
body:
When reviewing observations from a supplied dataset.

## Evidence to gather

Original observations, identity keys, units and any source-linked corrections.

## Review procedure

1. Identify the claim and trace its required fields to the records actually supplied. Use the data dictionary and stable source locations to distinguish a subject, event, sample, replicate and reading. Record units, identity links and transformations where they affect interpretation. Preserve the original value and locator alongside any correction.

2. For each missing or disputed field, ask which conclusions depend on it. A reading can support one calculation while its attribution to a particular source remains unresolved. Show which observations enter each conclusion and why. Avoid silently discarding usable measurements or filling missing fields from plausibility.

3. When a note conflicts with a record, inspect its author, timing, scope and the lab’s correction or reconciliation procedure. An authorized, traceable amendment may supersede an earlier field. An unsupported note can justify an investigation. Cite both records, state what survives under either reading, and identify the smallest missing link that would change the decision.

## Expected result

Traceable conclusions, affected records and unresolved attribution.

title: Claim-to-evidence review
description: Review a reported result against the research question, comparison units and underlying measurements.
body:
When reviewing a reported result against underlying measurements or a claim of certification against its cited source.

## Evidence to gather

The claim, its population and time window, and the underlying observations with identity keys.

## Review procedure

1. Translate the request into a quantity the evidence can answer. Identify the population, unit of observation, unit being compared, time window and intended units. Ask what gets one vote in the calculation. For change over time, determine whether the question concerns the same subjects or the populations observed at each time. State the relevant denominator and exclusions.

2. Trace the claim to its records and independently recompute it. Use identity keys for paired measurements. For grouped records, choose weighting from the research question and documented analysis plan. If two interpretations give materially different answers and the context cannot resolve them, give the conditional results or ask the narrow question that distinguishes them. Keep measured values, derived quantities and assumptions distinguishable.

3. Report what the records support, contradict or leave unresolved. Cite the decisive observations or reproducible selection and the lab context that justifies it. Explain what would change the decision and preserve conclusions unaffected by missing evidence. When a claim relies on certification, read the issuing source’s value table, qualifications and applicable revision. In the wording you would release, identify exactly which material or lot, property, value, units and uncertainty the issuer certifies, with any condition that changes its use. Give each other disputed value the status the source assigns it, such as a reference value, an estimate or a control result. If the supplied record only reports measurements, say what it establishes and what document would be needed to claim certification. A shared material name or an agreeing number does not extend the scope of a certificate.

## Expected result

Agreement, disagreement or a missing-evidence assessment with row references.
